thread:
Elaine: Heads up — seeing a reproducible latency regression (~40-60ms tail) for streaming responses in prod after the kernel-selector tweak last night. Symptoms: partial-decode handoffs that trigger kernel switches, plus higher KV cache miss rate during the stream window. PerfBot posted a flamegraph to #perf.

Mike: Which model and endpoint? rough % of requests affected?

Elaine: redwood/open-13b @ /v1/streams. Happening on ~2.4% of streaming requests, but those are concentrated on longer continuations (>= 80 tokens). P95 went from ~120ms -> ~165ms. KV miss rate during active stream went from 6% -> 18% in sampled traces.

Mike: Any logs showing the switch? can you paste a minimal trace?

Elaine: pasted one trace snippet from a failing session:

```
[06:12:03.112] admit request id=... kernel_hint=small-kernel-v2
[06:12:03.118] batch formed (n=3) -> selected kernel=wide-kernel-quant
[06:12:03.120] partial-decode send (stream) id=.. prefetch_kv_miss=true
[06:12:03.132] kernel switch cost=1.9ms kv_warmup=11.6ms total_extra=13.5ms
```

Jun: Looks like early flushes for streams are causing cross-kernel coalescing. Two levers we should consider:
- increase token_budget for streaming admission so streams stick in a forming batch longer (avoid early partial send)
- prefer kernel-affinity when coalescing streaming requests (prefer batching with same kernel to avoid switch)
- tighten prefetch window so KV warmups happen before decode handoff

Jun: rough config proposal (experiment):

```
batching:
  stream_token_budget: 64        # was 32
  kernel_affinity: prefer_same  # prefer coalesce by kernel
  prefetch_window_ms: 15        # was 8
  partial_decode_policy: allow-if-kernel-match
```

Anna: Increasing token_budget will increase latency for short streams/interactive small tokens — any perf numbers on how throughput changes?

PerfBot: profile summary (sampled 500 traces):
- kernel_switch_overhead: mean=1.8ms p95=3.2ms
- kv_warmup_miss_penalty: mean=11.7ms p95=29.4ms
- extra_copy/serialization: mean=2.1ms
- correlation: traces with partial-decode + kernel_switch have median extra latency = 14.2ms

Mike: That kv warmup is the killer. If kernel-affinity reduces switches by even 50% that beats small increase in batch latency. Also worried about fairness: streams waiting longer may impact low-latency clients.

Elaine: Agreed. Proposed A/B:
- A: stream_token_budget=64 + kernel_affinity=prefer_same (10% traffic)
- B: prefetch_window_ms=30 + partial_decode_policy=allow-if-kernel-match (10% traffic)
Monitor p50/p95 latency, KV miss rate on streaming sessions, and overall throughput.

Jun: I'll add a throttled fallback: if queue depth > 6, force early_send to avoid head-of-line stalls. Implementation note:

```
if queue.len > 6:
  early_send=true
else:
  early_send=token_budget_exhausted
```

Anna: Sounds good. How long for the A/B ramp and metric windows?

Mike: 48 hours should be enough with our current traffic to surface p95 changes. Run canary weekdays to avoid noise spike.

Elaine: I’ll own dashboards and perf alerts. Jun, can you land the config change behind a flag? PerfBot, re-run sampling after deploy and post flamegraphs.

PerfBot: scheduled sampling job -> started. Will post flamegraphs to #perf and drop a short summary when done.

Jun: Will push change to canary flag `stream_kernel_affinity_experiment` today.

Elaine: thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. If we see KV warmup still high we'll consider aggressive pre-warming for top-10 long-stream prefixes.

Mike: +1. Also add a tracing tag for "kernel_hint" in stream traces so we can slice by hint vs selected kernel.

Elaine: added to next PR. :thumbsup
